slots.label: Triangle and hypotenuse
entries: A right-angled triangle: the legs a = 3 and b = 4 meet at the right angle, the right-angle marker sits between them, and the hypotenuse c is the unknown longest side.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Squares on the short sides
entries: Squares on the short sides: the square on a is 3² = 9 and the square on b is 4² = 16, holding 9 and 16 unit squares.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Square on the hypotenuse
entries: The square on the hypotenuse: the tilted square on c is filled exactly by the 9 unit squares and the 16 unit squares together, so c² = 25.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Root gives the length
entries: 9 + 16 = 25: c is the square root of 25, so c = 5 - the lengths themselves add to 7, but it is the squares that the theorem adds.
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

slots.label: Hypotenuse
entries: The longest side of a right-angled triangle, across from the right angle: length 5 in the 3-4-5 triangle, found as c in a² + b² = c².
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Right-angled triangle
entries: A triangle with one angle of exactly 90 degrees, marked by the small square in the corner: the legs 3 and 4 meet at that right angle in the animation.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Square root
entries: The positive length whose square gives the number: the square root of 25 is 5, which turns c² = 25 back into the length c = 5.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

slots.label: Converse
entries: The theorem run backwards: if the squares of the two shorter sides add to the square of the longest side, as 9 + 16 = 25 does for sides 3, 4 and 5, then the triangle must be right-angled.
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.
